title: Learned Network Dynamics for Model Predictive Traffic Signal Control under Incidents
abstract: arXiv:2611.27435v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) of urban traffic signals relies on a model of how queues respond to signal decisions, which is hard to specify and calibrate in heterogeneous networks, particularly when incidents change capacities and turning shares. Measurements add a second limitation: the controlled lanes at the stop line are often short, so queues extending upstream of them fall outside lane-level measurements. We propose GNN-MPC, a receding-horizon controller that plans with action-conditioned network dynamics learned by graph neural networks. Phase sequences are coordinated across intersections by approximate best responses, with an acceptance test that keeps the predicted cost no higher than that of the initial plan. In microscopic simulation under non-recurrent incidents, GNN-MPC reduces travel time and increases completed trips relative to all tested controllers, on a homogeneous grid and a heterogeneous 21-intersection network. C

translated_title: 基于学习的网络动态用于事故情境下的模型预测交通信号控制
translated_abstract: 城市交通信号的模型预测控制（MPC）依赖于一个描述排队如何响应信号决策的模型，该模型在异构网络中难以指定和校准，尤其是在事故改变道路通行能力和转向比例的情况下。测量手段还存在第二个局限：停止线处的受控车道通常较短，因此向上游延伸的排队超出了车道级测量范围。我们提出GNN-MPC，一种滚动时域控制器，利用图神经网络学习到的动作条件化网络动态进行规划。相位序列通过近似最优响应在各交叉口之间进行协调，并设有接受性检验以保证预测成本不高于初始方案的成本。在非重复性事故的微观仿真中，无论在同质网格网络还是异构的21交叉口网络上，与所有测试过的控制器相比，GNN-MPC都降低了旅行时间并增加了完成的出行次数。
tldr: 提出GNN-MPC控制器，利用图神经网络学习动作条件化的网络动态并结合近似最优响应协调信号相位，在事故干扰下有效降低旅行时间并增加完成的出行次数。
en_tdlr: Proposes GNN-MPC, a receding-horizon traffic signal controller that learns action-conditioned network dynamics via graph neural networks and coordinates phases through approximate best responses, reducing travel time and increasing completed trips under non-recurrent incidents.
